description.value: The Richmond Museum is a free, City of Richmond-operated local history museum situated inside the Richmond Cultural Centre alongside the Brighouse branch of the Richmond Public Library. It explores the community's layered history — from Coast Salish First Nations to canneries and aviation — through exhibits and free self-guided walking tours covering three historic districts. A touring cyclist stopping here gains a grounded sense of the delta landscape they are riding through, plus downloadable PDF tour routes for the surrounding neighbourhoods.

The website's /visit/ subpage notes 'accessible parking is steps away' but makes no mention of bike-specific infrastructure, washrooms, water refill, or any cyclist amenity, leaving those fields unverifiable from available evidence. The about-this-site page surfaces a contact email (museum@richmond.ca) not present in the OSM record, and the group-visits page references 2023 booking language suggesting some site content is not fully current.
